questions.explain: The chapter defines the AI layer's input contract as a five-minute scheduled snapshot of distribution agent latency/throughput, CDC capture latency, and AG redo queue metrics stored in history tables — that history is the training data for every model.
options: A real-time CDC stream into a data lake
A five-minute scheduled snapshot of agent latency, throughput, CDC capture latency, and redo queues into history tables
A daily backup of the distribution database
An extended events session capturing every replicated statement
questions.q: What telemetry contract does the chapter require before any ML model is built for replication/CDC monitoring?

questions.explain: Cyclical time encodings let the model learn what normal latency looks like at 2 AM versus 2 PM, so seasonal batch spikes are ignored while genuinely anomalous climbs are flagged.
options: Cyclical encodings of hour-of-day and day-of-week so the model learns seasonal baselines
The SQL Server Agent job schedule IDs
The publication creation dates
The subscriber server time zones
questions.q: Why does the replication latency anomaly model encode time-of-day and day-of-week as cyclical features?

questions.explain: A stalled CDC capture job blocks log truncation (log_reuse_wait_desc = 'REPLICATION'), so the transaction log grows until the disk fills; the thirty-minute forecast buys time to restart the job before that happens.
options: The distribution database will run out of space for tracer tokens
Subscribers will permanently lose their subscriptions
The Query Store will stop collecting runtime stats
A stalled capture job blocks log truncation and the transaction log can fill the disk
questions.q: Why does the chapter treat predicted CDC capture lag as a severity-1 early warning?

questions.explain: When multiple subscribers degrade in a correlated way, the fault is upstream; computing pairwise correlation of per-stream anomaly scores grouped by publisher turns several pages into one incident with a located cause.
options: Restart every distribution agent simultaneously
Correlate per-stream anomaly scores grouped by publisher to localize the fault upstream
Increase the static latency threshold to reduce noise
Fail over the availability group
questions.q: When several subscribers degrade at the same time, what does the topology correlator recommend?

questions.explain: Shadow mode logs what the automation would have done for a month; a playbook is promoted to autonomous execution only when the log shows its decisions matched the human's at least 90% of the time.
options: One month of shadow-mode logging showing at least 90% agreement with human decisions
Approval from the application team
A successful failover test
Rewriting the playbook in T-SQL instead of Python
questions.q: What evidence does the chapter require before a remediation playbook is promoted from shadow mode to autonomous execution?

title: AI for Replication and CDC Monitoring
